noteRead.text:
How to read this canvas

Start with the Handoff board on the left: the arc, what changed on each screen and why, how each check was verified, the conflicts we ruled on and the lines that need sign-off.

Every screen is interactive. The panel on the right of a selected board has tweaks for its states (empty, error, offline and so on).

Three switches are marked as simulators, S1 to S3. The first option is our pick; the second is worth an A/B test because a metric should decide it.

The v38 artefact is untouched. This is a separate artefact.

noteS1.text: Simulator S1, how the draft is built. Default: live draft beside the text. Test against: a short interview of up to three skippable questions. Decided by draft completeness against time to submit and drop-off.

noteS2.text: Simulator S2, similar ideas. Default: a quiet nudge, decided on this screen. Test against: check first, a comparison before Review on a strong match. Decided by duplicates reaching the review desk against completion rate.

noteS3.text: Simulator S3, phone entry. Default: type first, with a large mic. Test against: voice first. Decided by phone completion and how often people correct the transcript.

noteReview.text:
How questions and decisions work

Meera from the review desk opens an idea (R2). Her main path is to decide straight away, after revising what it’s worth if she sees more in it than the sharer did. Asking first is optional and folded away: she picks from the questions reviewers usually ask, or writes her own. Each question points at a part of the idea (The problem, How often, Who it affects, What it’s worth, Attached or Fix), by the same name Kavya sees on her own page. She sets the time to answer.

Kavya answers only on Answer (R3, and its phone version): one question at a time, typed or spoken. Each answer lands on its part of her idea and posts back into the idea’s conversation (8) as one message. Elsewhere the questions show as a card with an Answer button, never a free-text box.

Either way, Meera decides on the same page: Pick, Not now or Not picked, each with a reason Kavya reads at once. The Ones Committee (R4) sees every decision for 30 days and can reverse it with a note to Kavya, or extend the window 30 days at a time up to 3 months. Then it expires and the decision stands.

noteH1.text:
H1 · Needs you, retired

The Inbox (H5) is now the one list of what waits on you, and Needs you is its tab. Home shows the top two with “All 3 in Inbox”. Each idea keeps its own conversation (8), so nothing is listed in four places and read state agrees everywhere.

noteLoad.text:
Draft loader (4, 4b and both phone boards)

The draft is built by six independent services, called together the moment your words arrive: title and summary, how often, who it affects, what it’s worth, area, and similar ideas. Each part shows a skeleton until its service answers.

How the bar moves
• Each service has a mean response time: p50 over the last 7 days, from monitoring. Prototype values: title 1.8 s, how often 0.9 s, who 1.2 s, worth 1.5 s, area 0.7 s, similar ideas 2.6 s.
• Weight = its share of the summed means: similar ideas 30%, title 21%, worth 17%, who 14%, how often 10%, area 8%.
• While a part waits, it rises along 0.9 × (1 − e^(−t ÷ mean)). It keeps moving and never fills on its own.
• When a part answers, it counts as full and its value fades in.
• The bar is the weighted sum, so it never pauses or moves back. It stays under 97% until all six are in.
• Time left comes from the slowest pending mean. A part past 1.5 × its mean says so, for example “still looking for similar ideas”.
• Move to Review waits for all six.

Loader tweak: Plays once, Slow similar ideas (3 × its mean), Held for review.
